'''''Leucophyta''''' is a plant [[genus]] which is endemic to [[Australia]].  The genus was first formally described by botanist [[Robert Brown (botanist, born 1773)|Robert Brown]] in 1818.<ref name=brown/>

The sole species in the genus is '''''Leucophyta brownii''''', also known as '''cushion bush'''.<ref name=vicg/> In 1891, German botanist [[Otto Kuntze]] assigned a number of species to this genus in his publication ''[[Revisio Generum Plantarum]]'' but none of his name combinations have currency, those species being presently divided between the genera ''[[Balladonia (plant)|Balladonia]]'', ''[[Blennospora]]'', ''[[Calocephalus]]'' and ''[[Gnephosis]]''.<ref name=apni1/><ref>{{cite web | title=Balladonia P.S.Short |publisher= [[Royal Botanic Gardens Kew]] | website=Plants of the World Online | url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:77166766-1 | access-date=6 December 2022}}</ref>

''Leucophyta brownii'' is a small, rounded shrub with tangled tomentose branchlets that give it a silvery appearance.<ref name=costermans/> Although it can grow up to a metre high, it is more usually 0.2 to 0.7 metres high.<ref name=vics/> It produces flowers during summer (December to February in Australia), which are white-yellow globular heads and about 1 cm in diameter.<ref name=wa/>

The species is common in cultivation in Australia, with a selected dwarf form from [[Tasmania]], known by the [[cultivar]] name 'Silver Nugget', also grown.<ref name=burke/>

==Habitat==
''Leucophyta brownii'' is found in coastal environments. It commonly occurs on the exposed faces of cliffs and dunes on the south coast of Australia.<ref name=costermans/><ref name=wa/> It is highly tolerant of prevailing winds, sea spray, drought and frost, and grows on predominantly sand or sandstone derived soil. Further, the soil can be highly alkaline when sand is composed of calcium carbonate. It grows most successfully in full sun.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Spencer |first1=Robert |title=Horticultural Flora of South-Eastern Australia. Volume 4. Flowering plants. Dicotyledons. Part 3. The identification of garden and cultivated plants. |date=2002 |publisher=University of New South Wales Press |isbn=0868406848}}</ref>
